events.title: The Synod of Worms and the Investiture Controversy
events.shortBlurb: King Henry IV and the German bishops declared Pope Gregory VII deposed, igniting the great struggle over investiture…
body: At Worms on 24 January 1076 the German king Henry IV, defying Pope Gregory VII's decrees against lay investiture and the excommunication of his counselors, gathered the bishops of his realm and renounced all obedience to the pope, declaring Hildebrand deposed from the see of Peter.

Henry's letter to Rome, addressed to Hildebrand, at present not pope but false monk, bade him descend, descend from the apostolic throne. Gregory answered at the Lenten synod that February: he excommunicated the king, declared him deprived of his throne, and released every Christian from the oath of allegiance sworn to him.

The blow shook the kingdom. The Saxons rose again in revolt, and in October 1076 the German princes assembled at Tribur gave the king a year to free himself of the ban on pain of losing his crown, inviting Gregory to judge the quarrel at Augsburg. To keep his throne Henry crossed the winter Alps to seek absolution.
